title: Her mother Virginia Burley and the first melodies on her lap
summary: Her mother played church piano and organ; Mary Lou picked out melodies at 2 or 3 and her mother called the neighbours. Professional pianists like Jack Howard were brought in to play around her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now your mother. What was her name?

Virginia Burley, B-u-r-l-e-y. She was born in Atlanta, Georgia, and she played piano for the church, danced for the church to raise money. She said that they'd pull a curtain down across the pulpit and she'd dance to raise money for the church and she also played for the church. When I was around between 2 and 3 she said I was always getting into things as a child, was a nervous baby. She was nervous all the time she was practicing the organ so she decided to put me on her lap while she was practicing. She said one day while she had me on her lap I started picking out melodies. It must have been unusual because she dropped me and ran out to call the neighbors to come in and hear it. From that day on she had professional musicians around me like Jack Howard. He was a terrific boogie-woogie pianist you see, who played rag-time. This was in Atlanta, Georgia. I was still there. I didn't leave Atlanta until I was

around 4, 5, or 6. You lose track of the dates and age but I know that I was at least 4 or 5. So she had Jack Howard and professional musicians to come in. I like Jack Howard because he played such a strong piano he could break up all the pianos and as a baby I started playing like that. I think I got the masculine quality from him, of playing.
